name: QAR overall: QS1's sub-metrics weighted by its ideals, with floor and ceiling
scoped_purpose: Measures how far QAR as a whole is from its ideals by combining the sub-metrics QME1 to QME7, each normalised to the range zero to one by a stated rule (pass rate; pass rate scaled by cost per passing turn; the share of solutions whose selection follows a current row) and weighted by the ideals of QS1: a weight per ideal with its reason in esoi.toml [balance.metric-qar-overall], split equally over the sub-metrics that serve it. Each sub-metric has a cheap tier (offline arms, or a small sampled run of a paid arm) for the everyday QUICK score and a full tier (the whole input set, against a live model where the arm is paid, run only by decision with a budget) for the FULL score. It is computed from recorded rows only and never re-runs an arm; an arm whose row is stale, missing or not built is unmeasured and never counted as a pass.
record: Per tier: the headline (the weighted value over the measured weight only), the floor (unmeasured counted as zero), the ceiling (unmeasured counted as one) and the measured share of the weight; per sub-metric its value, tier, and the date, commit and cost of each arm's last row; and what is not measured, with the command and estimated cost that would measure it, all printed by the command. The results row counts the sub-metrics measured on current rows and at or above the bar in esoi.toml. Re-run it after any results change: it costs nothing.

name: Cards per source-file group and duplicate share after repeated nested bootstrap
scoped_purpose: Measures, offline, whether a card store holds one card per distinct topic of its source files, on fixture stores inflated the way copy mode inflated real ones: two stores, one nested in the other's corpus, copying each other's current cards for a stated number of bootstrap passes, plus a taught card and a managed card, and in some cases two bootstrap cards for one topic pinning the same file, a card a person wrote with no provenance, a note a run added to a compounded copy, and two distinct topics of one file. A group is the files a card pins together with its topic name, so two distinct topics of one file are two groups. The card_store_growth arm builds stores through repeated passes with the library's guards and the runner's shipped settings. Each arm on the same cases, including the deliberately broken baseline (esoi run card_growth --impl card_growth.broken.drop_every_import:build, run by hand because a metric command names arms under impls/ only), one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the cases hash, with no model call. name: Mixed card and specification selection, with both existing selection metrics held
scoped_purpose: Measures whether one search puts the right cards and the right records in view together. Runs on a combined labelled set of requests and on the existing context_selection and spec_selection cases as its two halves, so a merged pipeline is compared with the two separate ones on the same cases. The combined set is evaluation/components/context_and_specs (generic fixture cards beside the spec_selection fixture index, with a problem and an intent that no solution serves and a fixture tag), with three kinds of request: ones whose right answer mixes a source (a file, a note, a conversation) and the solution, problem or metric it served; ones whose best match is a problem or an intent with no solution yet, labelled with that record and "no solution yet"; and ones that match only an ideal or a metric, labelled with the record a link should bring. The mixed set also holds a card alone, a solution alone, a runbook, a file with a failing metric, paraphrases, a past conversation, a change named by a tag (R3), two overlapping solutions (R1), an unrelated request, a note with its problem and an implementation's name; an ambiguous request is live only. The offline arms call no model; the two halves are not yet run for the merged arm.
record: Per arm on the same cases: the mixed-case pass rate (every expected card and record present, no more than the ceiling returned, the "no solution yet" mark where expected), the spec_selection balanced score and the context_selection pass rate on their own cases, and model calls per assembly; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. An arm that drops either existing metric does not win.
command: esoi run context_and_specs --impl two_pipelines; esoi run context_and_specs --impl solutions_and_problems_with_links

name: Right solution missed without the tag
scoped_purpose: Measures whether the tags identify the solutions a change must consult, in two parts. Recorded now, offline: the mechanical half of the first milestone, on fixture tag files (evaluation/components/tag_solutions): the rule passes a good file and fails each fault a person can make without judgement (a tag with no problem link, with no meaning, on every solution, used by none, linking a problem id that is not a record, a tag outside the list, a problem id copied into the tags column), and the lookup finds a solution through its tags and through its connected problems. Planned and unmeasured until search-cards-and-specs and its labelled requests exist: whether each tag mitigates the problems it links, as the share of labelled requests where a solution that covers or constrains the change is missed with the tags and with each tag removed in turn; a tag whose removal misses nothing more is retired.
record: Offline part: per case, the rule's problem lines and notes against the faults the case names, or the solutions the lookup returns; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash, with no model call, and the deliberately broken baseline (esoi run tag_solutions --impl tag_solutions.broken.membership_only:build, run by hand because a metric command names arms under impls/ only) must fail. Planned part: per tag, the share of labelled requests where the right solution is missed without it, against the share with all tags.

name: Copies kept out with real material kept in, by review availability
scoped_purpose: Measures, offline, what a lane takes in when its corpus root sits above a backups folder of dated snapshots, each carrying a card store and a copy of the corpus's nested store, beside one legitimate nested store and an ordinary docs folder. The solution is installed at the gate seam the bootstrap and the walk ask, and the library's real bootstrap runs in copy mode and in mount mode, with the folder review unavailable (no provider), switched off, failing on every call, answering skip for the snapshots, or answering index for everything; plus a corpus over the review's file-count floor, a person's index verdict in folder_review.json, a pair of snapshots, and a lone snapshot (kept as a known gap). The review's answers are fixed per case, so what is measured is how each implementation acts on each verdict, not whether a model judges a folder rightly. Read in this direction: series cards, mounts and open snapshot folders toward none where they should be kept out, with nothing real lost and no index verdict overruled.
record: Per case: cards imported or stores mounted from the series, snapshot folders the walk may enter, whether the nested store was taken in, whether the docs folder stayed indexed, and the folder review calls answered; a case passes when the series is kept out (or, under an index verdict, let in) and the nested store and docs are kept. One row per arm in the results log pinned to the commit and the cases hash, with no model call; the index-everything baseline is run by hand (esoi run choose_what_to_index --impl choose_what_to_index.broken.index_everything:build) because a metric command names arms under impls/ only.
command: esoi run choose_what_to_index --impl risk_gate; esoi run choose_what_to_index --impl review_only
